extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and applicants in chemical/polymer/textile fields
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examination criteria for patentability, sufficiency of disclosure, claim drafting, novelty and inventive step for alloy, polymer, polymer-composition, and textile inventions. Aimed at assessing and preparing patent applications in materials/chemical fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of numerical limitations (support/new matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amended numerical range (e.g., changing 200-10000㎛ to 200-6000㎛) is allowable if the amended numerical limit is included in or is specified as appropriate in the original specification and thus is not added as new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: reducing an upper limit is acceptable when the amended upper limit (6000㎛) is already specified/implicitly supported in the original specification or is within a composition range disclosed; the amendment is not considered addition of new matter when the amended range is included in the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity criteria for alloy novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity of an alloy invention is determined by whether each element of the alloy is identical and whether its composition range and structure are considered identical; also whether its utility (property or use) is identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: identity is determined by element composition, composition range, and property/use. For manufacturing methods of alloys, identity of both the alloy and the manufacturing process should be considered (see cited case law). Provided that utility limits that a specific composition or structure, the statement may be construed to specify the alloy invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining identity when composition and structure identical but perceived property/use differs
rubrics_metrics.description: If composition and structure of an alloy in the claimed invention and prior art are identical, then the inventions are substantially identical even if perceived properties or uses are stated differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if prior art does not disclose a use, the prior art composition/structure may be appropriate to that use; mere difference of use or limitation of use generally does not overcome anticipation. To be patentable based on different technical objectives despite identical configuration, the invention must correspond to a novel-use invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining identity when composition identical but structure depends on manufacturing method
rubrics_metrics.description: When alloy compositions are identical but structure is not disclosed in prior art, structure (which depends on manufacturing method) must be considered; if the same manufacturing method is applied to the same composition, the inventions are substantially identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because alloy structure can change with heat treatment or other processing, identity requires considering manufacturing method. If both composition and manufacturing method are the same, identity follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different structure/property/use can confer novelty despite identical composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if alloy compositions are identical, inventions having different structures, properties, or uses are not to be recognized as the same inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: two Fe alloys with same composition but different micro-lamellar structure yielding different suitability (piano wire vs cogwheel) are different inventions when specification and ordinary skill indicate structural differences and resulting properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived property differences that fall within existing utility do not create novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: If a differently perceived property of an alloy does not produce a new use but is included within existing utility, the inventions are substantially the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: two alloys with overlapping composition ranges and essentially the same properties/uses (heat-resisting alloy vs electrical resistance material with overlapping component ranges and utilities) are substantially the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive-step criteria for alloy inventions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine inventive step of an alloy invention, consider alloy composition and necessary structure; utility of the alloy (specific property or use); and specific means (manufacturing method) to obtain structure or utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assessment must examine composition, structure, utility, and manufacturing means together; all can contribute to inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of composition differences that typically lack inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: When an alloy differs from known alloys by (i) a different composition range, (ii) having an additional alloying element, or (iii) substitution with another alloying element, the invention does not involve inventive step unless the claimed alloy has significantly improved utility compared to the known alloy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: selecting 1-2% or 9-15% when prior art discloses 3-8% corresponds to (i); adding 0.05-0.5% of element B corresponds to (ii); substituting elements with known equivalent-purpose elements corresponds to (iii). Mere range shifts or substitution are insufficient without significant technical improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap/selection of composition ranges — criticality required
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of a specific composition range from a prior art composition range may be patentable only if that selection has critical technical meaning; partial overlap is often treated as identical unless critical significance is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law: even partial overlap can be deemed identical. The numerical limitation must have demonstrable technical significance; otherwise it is considered a selection without inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impurities and small amounts in prior art may negate novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace amounts of elements (e.g., Ti or Zr in 0.0002–0.500%) disclosed in prior art can be considered impurities and may fall within ranges considered as impurities in the claimed invention; skilled persons may adjust such amounts, undermining novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider whether those amounts are reasonably recognized as impurities and whether adjusting them would be technically difficult; if not, the claimed distinction may not be substantive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical limitations without technical significance are not inventive
rubrics_metrics.description: A numerical limitation (e.g., 'over 80% of TiB2 precipitates are single crystal' or specific Mn content) that lacks demonstrated technical significance or evidence of an effect is treated as a simple numerical selection and does not support inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification does not state technical significance or how to induce it, and no evidence shows qualitative or quantitative effect within that numerical range, the limitation is unlikely to confer inventive step. Case law cited where numerical limits were considered routine selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive-step assessment of different structure or utility
rubrics_metrics.description: If an alloy has similar structure or utility when composition is the same and manufacturing method is similar, the invention does not involve inventive step; conversely, demonstrable differences in structure or utility that are not obvious may support inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since alloy structure depends on manufacturing method, overlapping composition ranges with similar manufacturing conditions typically yield identical utility. Examiners must evaluate whether claimed structural features actually produce non-obvious advantages and require evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to describe polymeric compound sufficiently
rubrics_metrics.description: A particular polymeric compound should be described with specific explanation to sufficiently support the polymeric compound defined in claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is prerequisite to specify the polymeric compound because the technical element is the polymer; at least the main components such as atomic groups and molecular configuration must be clearly specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural requirements to specify polymers
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, specify polymeric compound by requirements representing its structure: (i) repeating units, (ii) arrangement of repeating units (homo, random, block, graft, head-to-tail coupling, etc.), (iii) molecular weight, (iv) local molecular properties (degree of branching, substituents, double bonds, degree of cross-linking, terminal groups, etc.), (v) stereo specificity (atactic, isotactic, syndiotactic, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, a linear organic polymer should be specified at least by the repeating unit and molecular weight. These structural descriptors are commonly used in chemistry to define polymers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quantitative basic properties when structure cannot be fully specified
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is difficult to specify the polymeric compound with structural requirements, requirements representing basic properties can be specified additionally and must be described in a quantitative manner (viscosity, crystallinity, glass transition temperature, melting point, density, tensile strength, elongation, modulus, hardness, impact strength, transparency, refractive index, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative property limits should be explicit so a skilled person can identify the polymer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding manufacturing method to clarify polymer definition
rubrics_metrics.description: If structure and basic properties are insufficient to specify the polymeric compound, its manufacturing method can be added as part of the specification to more clearly specify the polymeric compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturing steps, conditions, and relationships to structure/property should be described when needed to define the polymer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification data proving existence of polymeric compound
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification data proving the existence of the polymeric compound should be stated specifically for a person skilled in the art to easily and clearly recognize it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of identification data: elemental analysis, chemical bond analysis, glass transition temperature, refractive index, molecular weight, melting point, viscosity, infrared absorption spectrum, plasticity, and other physical or chemical properties. Measurement methods must be commonly used methods or be specifically described if non-standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to disclose manufacturing methods (polymers)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a person skilled in the art to easily synthesize the polymeric compound defined in the claim(s), at least more than one manufacturing method should be specifically described with essential matters such as source materials, manufacturing conditions and, if necessary, manufacturing devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples with specific numerical values and operating conditions should be provided so that the skilled person can carry out the process without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: If claim defines use of polymer, provide examples proving applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: If a use of a polymeric compound is defined in the claim, it is necessary to specifically describe at least more than one example which proves that the whole polymeric compound is applicable for the use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples showing the polymer as claimed performs the intended use across its claimed scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential elements of polymer manufacturing method claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention on a manufacturing method of polymeric compounds comprises three essential elements: (a) source materials, (b) processing means, (c) expected products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the source material is new, its manufacturing method should be described. Processing means (solvents, catalysts, reaction temperature/pressure/time) should be clearly described; examples with specific numerical values and operating conditions are required. If product is new, identify it and state physical/chemical properties proving its existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polymer composition disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention of a polymer composition should describe matters related to the composition itself and its use: (a) source materials and mixing ratio described specifically, (b) special features relating to state/property specifically stated, (c) embodiments with specific numerical values and operating conditions, (d) if source material is new, its manufacturing method described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe which property can be improved or newly obtained and state at least one use to prove utility. Utility is properly stated when use is objectively described, evident from properties, or obvious from objectives and technical features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming polymeric compounds (claim drafting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of polymeric compounds should particularly define the polymeric compound for which protection is sought; in principle by structure, and if not enough by basic properties or by including manufacturing method as partial definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claim scope should be supported by the description; structural descriptors are preferred as primary claim features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming manufacturing methods of polymers (claim drafting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of a manufacturing method of polymeric compounds must define the three essential elements (source materials, processing means, expected products) and the technical relationship between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims include sufficient detail so that the relationship among inputs, process, and outputs is clear to skilled persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming polymer compositions without functional limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: For polymer compositions claimed without limitation of function or use, components and their mixing ratio should be clearly defined; if not enough, chemical/physical state, properties or manufacturing method may be added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If components/mixing ratio cannot be determined, may define by starting materials composition but must supplement with phase transition or processing condition limitations if composition changes during processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming polymer compositions with functional/use limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: For polymer composition claims that include a function or use limitation, the function or use should be defined in addition to the components and their ratio which represent its utility overall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forms like 'Composition having a function of XX' or 'Composition for a use of XX'. If components/ratios inherently confer the function, the function limitation may be unnecessary; add it only when required to distinguish from other compositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description sufficiency for chemical-fiber inventions (textiles)
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions relating to chemical fiber characterized in material property, applicants must specifically state technical means including source material, structural characteristic of fiber, process conditions, and others to accomplish characteristics in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If insufficient details force excessive trial-and-error by skilled persons, the description is not enabling. Processing conditions like spinning, drawing, post-treatment must be described when they influence product characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description sufficiency for textile-structure inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions relating to textile structures (fabric, knit, etc.), if the structure is not a basic structure readily recognizable to a skilled person, the applicant must specifically state complete characteristics of the structure including repeating unit and manufacturing methods in description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full structural characterisation and production method so that the skilled person can reproduce the textile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive-step assessment for fiber from known polymer
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention using a linear polymer generally known for simply manufacturing fiber without other distinctive characteristics is deemed to lack inventive step; however, if selective composition or structure produces distinctive characteristics and utility not expected from the known polymer, inventive step may be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should determine whether the fiber exhibits unexpected properties arising from selective composition or structure beyond routine production from the known polymer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive-step assessment of parameter claims in fibers
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim specifies an invention on man-made fiber using a new parameter, it is necessary to compare manufacturing method and material properties (fiber strength, etc.) with prior art to determine whether the invention involves inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate that if prior art process variables would produce the parameter value or if the parameter merely describes an inherent property, the parameter claim may lack novelty/inventive step. Examiners should check whether parameter values are naturally obtained from prior art variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of method-specified fiber claims (breadth of properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: When construing a claim relating to fiber specified by a spinning method, the claim should not be limited to the embodiment in the description but should be construed to include the whole span of properties possible to produce according to the specified method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that recite a method should be read to cover the full range of outcomes the method can produce, not just the examples given, when assessing inventive step and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of textile inventions with design features
rubrics_metrics.description: Textile inventions characterized by design (exterior beauty) are evaluated subjectively; if the structure or processing method is obvious to a person skilled in the art or already described in prior art, the invention lacks inventive step. If design structure has a new technical function, patentability can be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the design produces technical function beyond ornamentation; mere aesthetic changes are insufficient if they are obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of effect from limited shape differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Minute differences of shape of textile components (ring, traveler, metallic card clothing, knitting needle, etc.) may greatly influence results, so the effect from any difference between the shapes must be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where effect is doubtful, test data or certified test results should be considered to substantiate claimed differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of textile inventions related to traditional art
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for traditional art (e.g., natural dyeing) may require searching non-patent documents since knowledge passed down traditionally may not appear in patent literature; compare improved traditional methods with prior art to determine inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should search non-patent literature and consider submissions (guidelines, catalogs) to assess novelty and inventive step accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of prior-art fields for textile machinery inventive-step search
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining inventive step of textile machinery, expand the scope of prior-art search to general machinery fields (not limited to textile IPC) because many textile inventions involve mechanical engineering known in general machine fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider non-patent documents such as device guidelines or catalogs; examine level of well-known prior art in general machine fields when assessing textile machinery inventions.
